title: How the Wealthy Game Disability Laws for Ivy League Gains — TikTok
notes: Story follows the article's arc: the elite numbers → what 504 plans give → the wealth gap in who claims them → the testing industry → West Virginia, where disability is a trap → the two-tiered system.
All figures are from the article (Apr 8, 2026) and the sources it cites (NCES, Department of Education, Census, the NYT analysis of 504 plans).

post.headline: How the wealthy game disability laws
post.caption: 38% of Stanford students are registered as disabled. In Weston, Connecticut, nearly 1 in 5 students claims a disability, eight times the rate 30 minutes away in Danbury. Meanwhile West Virginians on disability get by on $735 a month.
post.cta: Full story and interactive charts at the link in bio.

headline.text: {38%} of Stanford students are registered as disabled.

say: At Stanford, 38% of students are registered as disabled.
At Harvard and Brown, more than 20% of students are registered as disabled.
Elite schools accommodate the wealthy while often abandoning those who need support most.

scenes.title: Undergrads reporting a disability
say: At elite schools the share keeps climbing, and at the University of Chicago it more than tripled in eight years.
In Weston, Connecticut, where the median household income is $220,000, nearly 1 in 5 students claims a disability.

scenes.title: Students claiming a disability
say: Just 30 minutes north in Danbury, where the median income is $83,000, the rate is 8 times lower.

scenes.title: High school students with a 504 plan
scenes.subtitle: by district income
scenes.source: Department of Education · Census (via The New York Times)
say: Nationwide, high schools in the richest 1% of districts have almost four times the share of 504 students as the poorest.

overlays.label: per patient for a disability evaluation

scenes.source: Cognitive Assessment Group · How the Wealthy Game Disability Laws
say: One testing company charges $6,000 per patient, and about 70% leave with a diagnosis.
The stories of disability in West Virginia are very different, where 1 in 5 people has a disability, the highest rate of any state.

scenes.source: Social Security Administration · How the Wealthy Game Disability Laws
say: Donna Jean lives on disability in West Virginia, and her benefits pay her just $735 a month.

scenes.title: Americans with disabilities, compared with their peers
scenes.source: How the Wealthy Game Disability Laws · American Inequality
say: Americans with disabilities have a 3x higher unemployment rate and are 2x more likely to live in poverty.

items.headline: The disability accommodation trap on college campuses
items.dek: Disability accommodations were designed to level the playing field. At some elite colleges, they may now be reshaping the competition.

say: Medical diagnoses have become a luxury good for some while remaining an almost insurmountable challenge for others.

scenes.text: Disability support shouldn't depend on {the wealth of a ZIP code.}
say: Until we decouple disability support from the wealth of a ZIP code, this gap will keep widening.
You can read the full story on American Inequality.
